title: IS12:: helloworld.c (1.1)

lines.explanation: This is a comment. Comments are written not for computers but for humans. The computer will ignore everything between /* and */. Humans need comments to understand the program.
Empty lines separating parts of the program make it more readable
#include is a command which tells the compiler that the standard input / output  library will be used. Thus printf will be recognized as a standard output function
Empty lines separating parts of the program make it more readable
Execution of a C program always begins at the main() function. Every C program must have one (only one) main() function.
The open brace ({) marks the beginning of the function body, which is one or more program statements which perform some task

This statement is a function call to the printf function in the C Standard I/O Library. It displays the message which is the argument to the function. The    denotes the newline. We can use printf because we told the compiler to use Standard I/O Library.
The closing brace (}) marks the end of the function body
